rationale: The original Table 2 reports smaller paw thickness increases after two edible-part extracts and a seed extract. The study measures swelling and blood markers without a pain behavior endpoint.

The 48-rat paw comparison reports more edema suppression for Jihl than Bouskri at the reported timepoints. The methods and figure caption disagree on dosing. No pain outcome or whole-date exposure was measured.
The original abstract reports smaller paw volume and arthritis scores. Pain-specific outcomes and score components are unavailable at this access depth.
The orange juice component occurs in a mixed fermented-milk exposure. The animal outcomes address behavior and gut microbial profiles without isolating clinical bowel symptom changes from the fruit.
